outcome: Efficacy of BHGAL in controlling bleeding
cohort: This study retrospectively reviewed the records of 60 patients who underwent bilateral hypogastric artery ligation (BHGAL) for primary postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) after vaginal delivery or during/after cesarean section in a tertiary center between May 2005 and May 2018.
finding: Bilateral hypogastric artery ligation (BHGAL) was found to be more effective in controlling postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) due to uterine atony (89.2% success rate) compared to PPH from other causes (33.3% overall success rate).
mod_finding: While the study cohort included patients after vaginal delivery (VD) and during/after cesarean section (C/S), the findings regarding the effectiveness of BHGAL and complications were not specifically analyzed or presented stratified by the mode of birth.
